knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)

library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Niloy_2026b_MTMSATrp_mouse"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Niloy_2026b_MTMSATrp_mouse"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-026-04947-0> (open access)

Niloy et al. (2026) link drug exposure, tumor growth and survival for
MTMSA-Trp, a mithramycin analogue in preclinical development for Ewing
sarcoma, in a two-stage framework:

1. A **Simeoni tumor growth inhibition (TGI) model** (Eq. 1, Figure 1):
   exponential growth at rate `lambda0` that switches smoothly
   (exponent 20) to linear growth at rate `lambda1`, minus a direct kill
   term `k * Cp(t) * TV(t)`. `Cp` is the plasma concentration of the
   typical mouse from the group's one-compartment PK model with a
   dose-power effect on clearance (`modellib("Niloy_2026_MTMSATrp_mouse")`).
2. A **log-logistic time-to-event (TTE) model** (Eq. 2-3) for the
   model-derived time at which the predicted tumor volume reaches
   1500 mm^3. Its scale `Te` depends on the mouse's own `lambda0` and
   `lambda1` (each normalized by its median) and on the regimen average
   plasma concentration `Cavg`; the shape is 4.

Both stages are packaged in one model. The tumor volume is the state
`tumor_size` (observed with combined additive + proportional error);
`sur`, `cumhaz` and `hazard` are the TTE outputs, evaluated in closed
form at each output time.

# Population

The TGI model was fitted to 1377 tumor volumes from 104 female athymic
nude mice bearing subcutaneous TC-32 Ewing sarcoma xenografts: three
efficacy experiments pooled with historical vehicle controls, followed
for up to 100 days. Initial tumor volumes were 37-251 mm^3. MTMSA-Trp
was given as an IV bolus:

* Experiment 1: 0.3, 0.6 or 0.9 mg/kg once daily for 5 days (Q1dx5).
* Experiment 2: 2.40 mg/kg every 3 days for 6 doses (Q3dx6).
* Experiment 3: 2.40 mg/kg Q3dx6 and 2.85 mg/kg twice weekly for 6 doses
  (BIWx6).

The TTE dataset (Table S1) holds 62 mice of experiments 1-3: 54 events
and 8 right-censored (complete responders, plus one vehicle mouse whose
tumor did not grow).

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structural TGI equation | Simeoni growth with switch exponent 20, linear kill `k * Cp * TV` | Eq. 1; Figure 1 |
| `TV(0)` | observed initial tumor volume (regressor, `TUM_VOL`) | Results, TGI modeling |
| `lambda0` (`ltumorExpGrowth`) | 0.0063 1/h, omega 0.85 | Table 1 |
| `lambda1` (`ltumorLinGrowth`) | 5.93 mm^3/h, omega 0.73 | Table 1 |
| `k` (`ldrugSlope`) | 0.000024 mL/ng/h, omega 0.87 | Table 1 |
| Additive / proportional residual error | a = 11.22 mm^3, b = 0.22 | Table 1 |
| Log-logistic hazard | `h(t) = (s/Te)(t/Te)^(s-1) / (1 + (t/Te)^s)` | Eq. 2 |
| Covariate model on `Te` | `Te,pop * exp(b_l0 (l0/med - 1)) * exp(b_l1 (l1/med - 1)) * exp(b_Cavg Cavg/med) * exp(eta)` | Eq. 3 |
| `Te,pop` (`llambda`) | 703.17 h, omega 0.043 | Table 2 |
| `s` (`lgamma`) | 4, not estimated | Table 2; Table S6 note |
| `beta_lambda0` (`e_tumorExpGrowth_lambda`) | -0.75 | Table 2 |
| `beta_lambda1` (`e_tumorLinGrowth_lambda`) | -0.46 | Table 2 |
| `beta_Cavg` (`e_cav_lambda`) | 0.63 | Table 2 |
| PK: CL at 3 mg/kg, V, dose exponent | 39.18 mL/h/kg, 53.06 mL/kg, -0.30 | Niloy 2026 PK preprint Table 1 (reference [19] of the TGI-TTE paper) |
| `Cavg` | regimen NCA of the simulated typical PK profile | Methods, TTE modeling |
| Medians used to normalize `lambda0`, `lambda1`, `Cavg` | not printed; see Assumptions | -- |

# Regimens and regimen average concentration

`Cavg` is the average concentration over a dosing interval. With the
typical PK and a dose-dependent clearance, it is
`Dose / (CL(Dose) * tau)`, which is exact because MTMSA-Trp is cleared
within hours (half-life under 1 h) and nothing accumulates between doses.

```{r regimens}
cl_typ <- function(dose) 39.18 * (dose / 3)^-0.30 # mL/h/kg
cav_closed <- function(dose, tau) dose / (cl_typ(dose) * tau) * 1e6 # ng/mL

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,          ~dose, ~tau, ~n_doses, ~n_tte,
  "Vehicle",           0,     24,   0L,       13L,
  "0.3 mg/kg Q1dx5",   0.3,   24,   5L,       9L,
  "0.6 mg/kg Q1dx5",   0.6,   24,   5L,       10L,
  "0.9 mg/kg Q1dx5",   0.9,   24,   5L,       15L,
  "2.4 mg/kg Q3dx6",   2.4,   72,   6L,       8L,
  "2.85 mg/kg BIWx6",  2.85,  84,   6L,       7L
) |>
  mutate(
    CAV = ifelse(dose > 0, cav_closed(dose, tau), 0),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = treatment)
  )

knitr::kable(
  regimens |>
    rename(
      "Regimen" = treatment, "Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "Interval (h)" = tau,
      "Doses" = n_doses, "Mice in TTE dataset (Table S1)" = n_tte,
      "Cavg (ng/mL)" = CAV
    ),
  digits = c(0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 1)
)
```

The median `Cavg` over the 62 mice of the TTE dataset falls on the
0.6 mg/kg Q1dx5 regimen, which holds the 31st and 32nd mice when they
are ranked by `Cavg`. The model uses that value, 393.7 ng/mL.

```{r cav-median}
cav_per_mouse <- rep(regimens$CAV, regimens$n_tte)
med_cav <- median(cav_per_mouse)
med_cav
stopifnot(abs(med_cav - 393.7) < 0.05)
```

## PKNCA check of Cavg

The paper computed `Cavg` by noncompartmental analysis of the simulated
profiles. Repeating that with PKNCA on the packaged PK layer recovers the
closed form.

```{r pknca}
mod <- readModelDb("Niloy_2026b_MTMSATrp_mouse")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# Typical-value solves of several subjects: rxode2 warns that there is no
# omega to sample from, which is the intent here. Only that warning is
# muffled.
solve_typical <- function(events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events, ..., returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

treated <- regimens |> filter(dose > 0)
pk_events <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(treated)), function(i) {
  r <- treated[i, ]
  grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.02), seq(2, r$tau, by = 0.25))))
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = r$dose, cmt = "central"),
    data.frame(time = grid, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(id = i, COHDOSE = r$dose, CAV = r$CAV, TUM_VOL = 100,
           treatment = as.character(r$treatment))
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

pk_sim <- solve_typical(pk_events, keep = "treatment")

conc_df <- pk_sim |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))
dose_df <- pk_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
                             concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                             doseu = "mg/kg")
intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = as.character(treated$treatment),
  start = 0, end = treated$tau,
  cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                          intervals = intervals))

cav_check <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, cav_pknca = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(treated |> mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)) |>
              dplyr::select(treatment, cav_closed = CAV),
            by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (cav_pknca - cav_closed) / cav_closed)

knitr::kable(
  cav_check |>
    rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Cavg, PKNCA (ng/mL)" = cav_pknca,
           "Cavg, closed form (ng/mL)" = cav_closed,
           "Difference (%)" = pct_diff),
  digits = 2
)

# Same parameters on both sides: only trapezoid error remains.
stopifnot(all(abs(cav_check$pct_diff) < 1))
```

# Virtual cohort

Each regimen gets 150 virtual mice. The paper reports only the range of
initial tumor volumes (37-251 mm^3), so `TUM_VOL` is drawn log-normally
around 100 mm^3 and truncated to that range. Tumor volumes are followed
to 2400 h (100 days), the follow-up of the experiments.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)
set.seed(20261025)
n_per_arm <- 150L
t_end <- 2400

make_arm <- function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, t_end, by = 6))
  obs$evid <- 0L
  obs$amt <- 0
  obs$cmt <- "tumor_size"
  doses <- NULL
  if (r$n_doses > 0) {
    doses <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = (seq_len(r$n_doses) - 1) * r$tau)
    doses$evid <- 1L
    doses$amt <- r$dose
    doses$cmt <- "central"
  }
  tv0 <- data.frame(
    id = ids,
    TUM_VOL = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n_per_arm, log(100), 0.4)), 37), 251)
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(COHDOSE = r$dose, CAV = r$CAV,
           treatment = as.character(r$treatment)) |>
    left_join(tv0, by = "id")
}
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), make_arm))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "treatment",
                       returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = levels(regimens$treatment)))
```

# Tumor growth (Figure 3)

Median and 90% prediction interval of the simulated tumor volume
(`tumor_size`, without residual error) per regimen.

```{r fig3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
vpc_tv <- sim |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(tumor_size, 0.05), q50 = median(tumor_size),
    q95 = quantile(tumor_size, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc_tv, aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1500, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 2500)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Tumor volume (mm^3)",
       caption = paste("Replicates the shape of Figure 3 of Niloy 2026",
                       "(individual fits); dashed line = 1500 mm^3 endpoint."))
```

Vehicle tumors grow from about 100 mm^3 to the 1500 mm^3 endpoint in
about three weeks, the once-daily regimens delay regrowth in a
dose-ordered way, and the two high-dose regimens hold the tumor near
zero for weeks before some regrow, as in Figure 3.

```{r tgi-typical}
typ_tv <- solve_typical(
  events |> filter(id %in% ((seq_len(nrow(regimens)) - 1L) * n_per_arm + 1L)) |>
    mutate(TUM_VOL = 100),
  keep = "treatment"
)
typ_summary <- typ_tv |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    tv_240 = tumor_size[time == 240],
    t_1500 = suppressWarnings(min(time[tumor_size >= 1500])),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = levels(regimens$treatment))) |>
  arrange(treatment)
knitr::kable(
  typ_summary |>
    rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Typical TV at 240 h (mm^3)" = tv_240,
           "Typical time to 1500 mm^3 (h)" = t_1500),
  digits = 1
)

# Deterministic ordering of the typical mouse: more drug, later endpoint.
stopifnot(
  !is.unsorted(typ_summary$t_1500[1:4]),
  typ_summary$tv_240[typ_summary$treatment == "Vehicle"] > 300,
  all(typ_summary$tv_240[5:6] < 20)
)
```

# Time-to-event layer

## Closed-form checks

For the typical mouse (median `lambda0`, `lambda1`), `Te` is
`703.17 * exp(0.63 * Cavg / 393.7)`, and the log-logistic survival is
exactly 0.5 at `t = Te`. The cumulative hazard and hazard returned by the
model must agree with `-log(S)` and with its time derivative.

```{r tte-closed-form}
te_typ <- 703.17 * exp(0.63 * regimens$CAV / 393.7)
tte_events <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  data.frame(id = i, time = sort(c(seq(0, 3000, by = 50), te_typ[i])),
             evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "tumor_size",
             COHDOSE = r$dose, CAV = r$CAV, TUM_VOL = 100,
             treatment = as.character(r$treatment))
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
tte_typ <- solve_typical(tte_events, keep = "treatment")

at_te <- tte_typ |>
  group_by(id) |>
  filter(abs(time - te_typ[id]) < 1e-6) |>
  ungroup()
stopifnot(
  nrow(at_te) == nrow(regimens),
  all(abs(at_te$lambda - te_typ) < 1e-6 * te_typ),
  all(abs(at_te$sur - 0.5) < 1e-10)
)

pos <- tte_typ |> filter(time > 0)
stopifnot(all(abs(pos$cumhaz + log(pos$sur)) < 1e-10))

# hazard = d(cumhaz)/dt by a central difference at t = 600 h
h_num <- function(te, t, dt = 1e-3) {
  ch <- function(x) log(1 + (x / te)^4)
  (ch(t + dt) - ch(t - dt)) / (2 * dt)
}
h_600 <- tte_typ |> filter(time == 600)
stopifnot(all(abs(h_600$hazard - h_num(h_600$lambda, 600)) <
                1e-6 * h_600$hazard))

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Regimen = regimens$treatment, "Cavg (ng/mL)" = regimens$CAV,
             "Typical Te (h)" = te_typ, check.names = FALSE),
  digits = 1
)
```

## Survival by regimen (Figure 4b)

The paper's event is the TGI-predicted time for the tumor to reach
1500 mm^3, censored when it is not reached during follow-up. Two
quantities are compared per regimen:

* the survival curve of those **TGI-derived event times** in the virtual
  cohort (censored at 2400 h), which is the endpoint the TTE model was
  fitted to; and
* the **TTE-model** population survival, the mean over the same virtual
  mice of `sur(t) = 1 / (1 + (t / Te_i)^4)`, with each `Te_i` driven by
  that mouse's own `lambda0`, `lambda1` and the regimen `Cavg`.

```{r fig4b, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
event_times <- sim |>
  group_by(treatment, id) |>
  summarise(t_event = suppressWarnings(min(time[tumor_size >= 1500])),
            .groups = "drop")

surv_grid <- seq(0, t_end, by = 24)
tgi_surv <- event_times |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  reframe(time = surv_grid,
          surv = vapply(surv_grid, function(t) mean(t_event > t), numeric(1)))

tte_surv <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% surv_grid) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(surv = mean(sur), .groups = "drop")

ggplot() +
  geom_step(data = tgi_surv, aes(time, surv, colour = "TGI-derived event times")) +
  geom_line(data = tte_surv, aes(time, surv, colour = "TTE model"),
            linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TGI-derived event times" = "black",
                                 "TTE model" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Probability of survival", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4b of Niloy 2026 (final TTE model by regimen).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Median event times per regimen. The observed medians are read by eye
from the Kaplan-Meier curves of Figure 4b and are approximate; the
virtual cohort draws `lambda0` and `lambda1` from the whole TGI
population (including the historical controls), not from the mice of
each experiment, so agreement within a few hundred hours is what can be
expected.

```{r medians}
median_surv <- function(time, surv) {
  i <- which(surv <= 0.5)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) NA_real_ else time[i]
}
fig4b_obs <- c(700, 550, 800, 1450, 1900, 1500)

med_tab <- tgi_surv |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(tgi_median = median_surv(time, surv), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(tte_surv |>
              group_by(treatment) |>
              summarise(tte_median = median_surv(time, surv), .groups = "drop"),
            by = "treatment") |>
  arrange(treatment) |>
  mutate(fig4b_observed = fig4b_obs)

knitr::kable(
  med_tab |>
    rename("Regimen" = treatment,
           "Median, TGI-derived event times (h)" = tgi_median,
           "Median, TTE model (h)" = tte_median,
           "Median, Figure 4b observed (approx., h)" = fig4b_observed),
  digits = 0
)

# Centre check: a mis-transcribed growth rate, kill rate or TTE scale
# moves every regimen by a large factor. The vehicle and 0.6 mg/kg arms,
# which have the most events in Table S1, are compared with their observed
# medians; the bound leaves room for cohort-to-cohort variation of the
# simulated median.
ratio_vehicle <- med_tab$tte_median[1] / fig4b_obs[1]
ratio_06 <- med_tab$tte_median[3] / fig4b_obs[3]
stopifnot(
  abs(log(ratio_vehicle)) < log(1.75),
  abs(log(ratio_06)) < log(1.75)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Normalizing medians.** Eq. 3 normalizes `lambda0`, `lambda1` and
  `Cavg` by their medians, which the paper does not print. The medians of
  `lambda0` and `lambda1` are the medians of the post hoc estimates of
  the 62 TTE mice; the model uses the Table 1 typical values (0.0063 1/h
  and 5.93 mm^3/h) instead. Because Table S4 shows that the experiment
  mice grew more slowly than the historical controls that also inform the
  typical values, the true medians are probably somewhat lower, which
  would shorten the predicted `Te` of a mouse with a given growth rate.
  The median `Cavg` (393.7 ng/mL) is reconstructed from the PK model and
  the Table S1 group sizes, taking the median over mice as Monolix does
  for covariate centering.
* **Form of the Cavg term.** Eq. 3 prints `exp(beta_Cavg * Cavg / median
  Cavg)` without the `- 1` used for the growth rates; it is coded as
  printed, so `Te,pop` = 703.17 h is the scale at zero exposure
  (vehicle). The vehicle arm's simulated median (about 550 h) is close to
  the observed Figure 4b median (about 700 h), which supports this
  reading.
* **Cavg definition.** "Regimen-specific average concentration" is taken
  as the average over a dosing interval, `Dose / (CL(Dose) * tau)`.
  Because there is no accumulation, this equals the average over the
  whole dosing period. An average over the full 100-day follow-up instead
  would multiply the 2.4 and 2.85 mg/kg exposures by 4-7 and push almost
  every treated `Te` beyond follow-up, contradicting the events in
  Table S1.
* **PK layer.** The TGI paper simulated the typical PK profile of each
  regimen from the group's earlier PK model (reference [19]); its values
  (CL 39.18 mL/h/kg at 3 mg/kg, V 53.06 mL/kg, dose exponent -0.30) are
  taken from that preprint and held constant, with no PK variability, as
  in the paper. Vehicle mice carry `COHDOSE = 0`, and the model then uses
  the 3 mg/kg reference so that the unused clearance stays finite.
* **Residual error form.** Table 1 reports an additive `a` and a
  proportional `b` without saying how they combine. The model uses
  `combined1()` (standard deviation `a + b * f`), the Monolix default
  combined error model.
* **No IIV correlations** are reported; the three TGI random effects are
  independent.
* **Initial tumor volumes.** Only the range (37-251 mm^3) is reported;
  the virtual cohort's log-normal distribution around 100 mm^3 is an
  assumption, and it matters for the timing of the endpoint.
* **Censoring.** The paper censored animals that did not reach
  1500 mm^3 because their tumors had regressed completely. The TGI model
  has no eradication state, so a simulated tumor driven very low regrows
  later; the virtual cohort is censored at the 2400 h end of follow-up.
* The TTE stage describes a **model-derived** endpoint. As the paper
  stresses, its covariate effects follow from how the endpoint was
  defined and are not independent evidence that growth rates or exposure
  predict survival.
